note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), original in English. The affinities section of the original states that this species "may be distinguished from the other species by its distinctly larger size", which contradicts the "small" of the opening description; this is probably a printing error in the original and the description of the characters has not been rewritten on that basis.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original (Hill 1942) follows Heterotermes platycephalus Froggatt, 1896 (type locality Kangaroo Island, South Australia) and places Leucotermes clarhi Hill, described in 1922 from the soldier only (its alate was added in 1927), as a synonym. The alate is small and pale brown with long, narrow, pale brown wings; the soldier has a bright yellow head with nearly parallel sides.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: A small pale brown species with long, narrow, pale brown wings. Head clay-coloured, upper surface tinged pale brown, clypeus and legs slightly paler, wings pale yellowish brown. Head (Figs. 72, 73) small, slightly longer than wide, widest at the compound eyes, broadly rounded behind. Frons flat or slightly concave. Postclypeus small, about three-eighths as long as wide, hairless. Compound eyes small, nearly triangular (diameter 0.22—0.27), facets fine, usually not projecting beyond the sides of the head. Ocelli present (Froggatt 1896 called them absent), very small (length 0.07), separated from the compound eye by about half their length. Fontanelle small, circular, moderately distinct. Antennae 17—19-segmented; segment 3 usually the shortest, segment 4 slightly longer than segments 5 and 6. Pronotum far narrower than the head, anterior margin convex with a deeper median concavity, sides abruptly narrowed to the slightly concave posterior margin; posterior margins of mesonotum and metanotum broadly and deeply concave. Fore wing pad about one-third longer than the hind wing pad, not reaching the base of the hind wing pad. Wing length more than twice the rest of the body. Costa and radius sector of the fore wing stout; media nearer the cubitus than the radius, stout at the base and then becoming indistinct, usually with 2 or 3 branches; the proximal 5—7 branches of the cubitus well defined, the remaining 5—7 indistinct. Measurements: length with wings 13.00—14.00; length without wings 5.25—6.00; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.21—1.32; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.88—0.97; head width 1.02—1.10; pronotum length 0.51—0.55; pronotum width 0.80—0.91; fore wing length 11.40—12.50; fore wing width 2.67—2.82.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head bright yellow, palest posteriorly, base of mandibles bright yellow becoming dark rust-coloured anteriorly, labrum and antennae bright yellow, thorax pale yellow. Head (Fig. 74) with nearly parallel sides, sometimes slightly narrower posteriorly, fontanelle area slightly concave, anterodorsal projection distinct. Postclypeus slightly less than four times as wide as long. Fontanelle not very distinct. Vertex without wrinkles. Antennae 16—18-segmented; segment 3 the shortest; segment 4 longer than segments 5 and 6. Labrum large, about as long as wide at the base, sides almost not widening, conical in front. Anterior part of pronotum strongly convex with a deep median concavity, sides narrowed posteriorly, posterior margin deeply concave. Legs rather short and stout. Measurements: total length 5.75—7.50; head length (with mandibles) 2.89—3.26; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 1.83—2.05; head width 1.14—1.28; least width of postmentum 0.18—0.22; pronotum length 0.53—0.66; pronotum width 0.88—1.17.
